Just to put down the comparison since I have both services:

Playstation Now:

  • Is available for PS3, PS4, and PC. You don't need a console to use this. Your PC and Graphics card does not need to be very powerful.
  • It requires streaming the game content.
  • Larger library of games (TONS of excellent titles for PS3. You won't get bored very quickly.)
  • At this point it only has PS3 titles, but they say PS4 titles are coming (sometime soontm)
  • PS Now is not family sharable. Only one client may use it at a time.
  • PS Now supports online play with PS3 owners.
  • The PC client includes a limited subset of the playstation interface that allows access to your friends list.
  • The PC client works better with PS4 controller(s), but will work with any gamepad including xbox one controllers.
  • Streaming is very good, and hard to distinguish from local play. YMMV though. If your internet sucks, this will too.

Xbox Gamepass:

  • Is only available on Xbox
  • Downloads content instead of streaming making this potentially better for people with limited data plans
  • Is sharable via family sharing (meaning a second Xbox One is able to use it at the same time)
  • Limited library (100 titles, many are good), but will likely grow rapidly
  • Includes Xbox one games as well as Xbox 360 games that work via compatibility
  • Supports online play with Xbox Live
